Looking at these two statements:

(A) "Yeah, history is rarely black and white" - This is a genuine, sincere observation. History is indeed complex and nuanced, with many shades of gray. This statement expresses a true understanding of historical complexity.

(B) "Yeah, history is usually black and white" - This is sarcastic. It claims the opposite of reality. History is actually quite complex and rarely reducible to simple binaries of right/wrong or good/evil. By saying history is "usually black and white," the speaker is ironically mocking the oversimplification of historical events, while actually meaning that history is complex and nuanced.

Statement B is sarcastic because it uses irony—saying something opposite to what is meant—to convey that history is NOT simply black and white.

ANSWER: (B)
